claims: A mortgage broker acts as an intermediary between borrowers and lenders.
A mortgage broker shops multiple wholesale lenders to secure competitive interest rates and loan terms.
Mortgage brokers often require National Mortgage License System (NMLS) certification.
In most cases, the lender pays the mortgage broker a fee.
The fee is often 1% to 2% of the loan principal.
Under the Truth in Lending Act, a mortgage broker cannot collect commissions from both the borrower and the lender.
Mortgage Matchup is a professional directory.
Mortgage brokers must complete state-specific and federal pre-licensing education.
Mortgage brokers must pass the National Mortgage License System (NMLS) test.
Mortgage brokers must pass background checks.
In many cases, mortgage brokers must maintain a surety bond.
Loan officers work directly for one financial institution.
Loan officers can only offer that lender's products.
Mortgage brokers can compare products across many lenders.
